Fixture: 40_checker_64x64_lossless.jxl
64x64 RGB checkerboard (8x8 blocks), mathematically lossless, effort 1 --
nested-LZ77 constraint probe (C.2.2)

Purpose
-------
Aimed at NESTED_LZ77_REJECTS_ENABLED (jpxl-entropy/src/dist.rs): whether a
nested distribution decoder whose parent had num_dist == 2 rejects a stream
that sets lz77.enabled (this crate's reading) or silently overrides it. This
requires a real bundle with num_dist == 2 that chooses the general/nested
clustering encoding AND sets lz77.enabled on the nested decoder -- effort 1
(least optimisation, most literal) plus large flat 8x8-block runs is the most
LZ77-friendly content reachable through cjxl's CLI (there is no flag to force
LZ77 or a specific num_dist).

Result: negative. See docs/experiments/2026-08-03-flip-point-fixtures.md.
Decoding this fixture (and eleven siblings: this checkerboard plus thin
stripes and two-value noise, each at -e 1/3/9) never reaches
SymbolDecoder::open_nested with forbid_lz77 == true at all, let alone with
lz77.enabled == 1. The flip point remains unexercised; the constraint reading
stands as the safer default for attacker-controlled input.

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run of
tools/make-experiment-fixtures.sh).

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
